title: Shape the notes
learned: A note's length is how long the gate stays high: longer notes reach the envelope's sustain
QUANTIZE (Q) moves the notes onto the grid: tight timing from a loose take
Velocity is how hard a note is struck; Host MIDI sends it as a voltage you can patch anywhere
Copy and paste (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V) at the playhead repeats a part

steps.why: A melody you have drawn or played is a first draft. This lesson shapes one: length, timing, dynamics, repetition.
steps.do: A two-bar melody is in track 1, a little out of time, as if played by hand. Press F4 to open the Editor.
steps.after: Look at the notes against the grid lines: some start a little early, some a little late. LOOP is on, so bars 1 to 4 repeat (the second half is still empty).

steps.why: How long a note is decides how long the gate stays high, and so how the envelope plays it.
steps.do: Drag the right end of a note to the right to make it longer.
steps.after: A longer gate lets the envelope sit at its sustain level, a short one lets it fall into the release sooner: the same melody played legato or staccato. The next note you draw gets this length.

steps.why: Hand-played timing drifts. Quantizing moves each note to the nearest line of the grid.
steps.do: With the mouse over the roll, press Q (or click QUANTIZE at the top). With no note selected it quantizes the whole track.
steps.after: Every note jumped onto a grid line: the melody now plays tight. GRID sets which lines: 1/16 is fine, 1/8 coarser, the T grids are triplets. Quantize once you have recorded or drawn a part.
steps.try: Ctrl+Z brings the loose timing back; listen to both.

steps.why: Every note also carries a velocity: how hard the key was struck (1 to 127). Host MIDI sends it from its VELOCITY output as 0 to 10 V, but nothing in this patch listens to it yet.
steps.do: Press Esc. Drag VELOCITY of Host MIDI to jack 5 of the patchbay, press Tab and drag jack 5 to FREQ CV of the filter.
steps.after: Now a harder note opens the filter further: velocity became brightness. Velocity is just a voltage: it could open an amplifier, change a decay, anything.

steps.why: Now you can hear velocity: give the melody accents.
steps.do: Press F4. In the VEL lane at the bottom, drag the bars of some notes down.
steps.after: Softer notes sound darker, the loud ones stand out: accents make a line feel played rather than typed. Drag a bar up to make a note louder again.

steps.why: Music repeats: a part you like is copied and then varied.
steps.do: With the mouse over the roll, press Ctrl+A to select all notes and Ctrl+C to copy them. Press Space to pause, click bar 3 in the ruler above the roll (its upper half, with the numbers) to move the playhead there, press Ctrl+V and then Space.
steps.after: The copy landed at the playhead: bars 3 and 4 now repeat bars 1 and 2. Pasting again puts the next copy right after it.
steps.try: Change two or three notes of the copy, so the second half answers the first.

steps.do: Length, timing, velocity and repetition shape a melody. Press Esc and then Next to finish.
